subject: Approval request: 3yr rate-securitization + renewal protection (Novamed)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Approval request: 3yr rate-securitization + renewal protection (Novamed)

Team —

Quick context: Novamed (healthtech customer) is warming up to a 3-year commitment. They want a multi-year price lock and an express renewal protection clause (limits uplift on renewal). Key commercial asks:

- 3-year term, target ACV $1.18M year 1 (with 8% planned growth in usage year-on-year)
- One-time onboarding professional services in year 1 (SOW attached)
- 25% upfront discount off our public list for year 1 (they asked for 30%)
- Price lock across 3 years with an annual uplift cap of 4% and a renewal protection clause that prevents >6% increase at renewal (Novamed wants an explicit clawback if we lift >6%)
- They propose a small escrow to backstop the renewal protection: $200k deposited at signature, refundable if we honor the uplift cap at renewal; they want this reflected in the contract.

Why escalate: the 25% discount + the escrow mechanics + the refresh renewal protection are outside standard Deal Desk guardrails (discount >20% and novel escrow language). This will set a precedent if we accept the escrow model as a commercial lever.

Ask: approval to offer the below compromise to close in next 2 weeks:
- Approve up to 25% discount for year 1 (structured: 20% list discount + an additional transaction-level 5% concession)
- Approve price lock with 4% annual uplift cap and a renewal protection clause that guarantees renewal uplift will not exceed 6% without exec sign-off
- Approve escrow mechanics capped at $150k (counter-proposal to Novamed's $200k) to be held in Redwood-controlled escrow account and returned if uplift cap honored; finance/legal to own handling

If approved I will:
- Ask Karthik to draft the specific escrow and renewal language for Legal review
- Ask Ben for a quick ARR / cashflow impact note to validate finance comfort
- Ask Marissa for go/no-go given revenue/strategic context

Attachments: Novamed_SOW_v2.pdf, redwood-rate-shield-draft.docx (draft commercial language)

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval request: 3yr rate-securitization + renewal protection (Novamed)

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear write-up. High level: I support a path to close here — Novamed is strategic in the payer integrations space and the 3yr commit drives stickiness. Two asks before I greenlight:

1) Finance (Ben) needs to confirm ARR/NRR impact and P&L timing on the proposed escrow and the incremental concession mechanics.
2) Legal/Deal Desk (Karthik) should provide a short memo on precedent risk for a refundable escrow tied to pricing protection (we don't typically accept third-party escrow that conditions refunds on our price behavior).

If Ben and Karthik are comfortable with the $150k cap and we include an explicit exec sign-off for any renewal adjustment >6%, mark me tentatively approved.

Marissa
VP, North America Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval request: 3yr rate-securitization + renewal protection (Novamed)

Marissa / Jordan —

I ran a quick sensitivity against the model: at 25% year-1 discount with 4% annual uplift cap, our 3yr NPV is down ~12% vs list, and cashflow improves slightly because of reduced churn risk. The escrow at $200k is more than I'd like; $150k is tolerable.

Counter-proposal I can sign off on (pending final legal wording):
- Approve effective discount up to 25% year 1, but require a revenue protection addendum: if realized usage growth exceeds our forecast by >15% in any year we reserve right to revisit pricing (not apply retrospectively) — this protects unit economics against runaway usage spikes.
- Escrow capped at $150k, Redwood to manage escrow account; funds refunded on renewal if uplift cap honored.

Karthik — please confirm whether escrow wording will require additional accounting treatment or impact how we recognize revenue for year 1 services. If so, escalate to Finance Ops.

Ben
Head of Finance
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval request: 3yr rate-securitization + renewal protection (Novamed)

Team —

I've attached a marked-up draft (redwood-rate-shield-draft.docx) with suggested language. Key notes:

- Escrow mechanics: recommend escrow be Redwood-controlled with a payer instruction schedule; avoids third-party escrow complexity. We should document clear release triggers (e.g., indexed to the executed renewal amendment and signed confirmation that uplift did not exceed 6%).
- Renewal protection: propose a capped remedy (refund of escrow up to $150k + credit against the first month of renewal fees) rather than an open-ended clawback to limit operational exposure.
- Usage spike protection: Ben's suggestion to include a usage-growth trigger is reasonable — we can include a tiered commercial adjustment clause if consecutive quarters exceed forecast by >15%.

Legal is comfortable with this structure if Finance confirms no material accounting/recognition impact. I can loop Legal in for final language and prepare a DocuSign envelope once approved.

DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.net/HH64jk2

Karthik Iyer
Director, Deal Desk & Pricing
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Rios <evelyn.rios@novamed.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval request: 3yr rate-securitization + renewal protection (Novamed)

Jordan / Redwood team —

Thank you — Novamed appreciates the collaborative approach. We can accept the counter-proposal with the following confirmations:

1) Escrow capped at $150k (Novamed will fund at signature)
2) 25% year-1 discount as structured (we accept 20% list + 5% transaction concession)
3) Renewal protection with uplift cap of 6% and escrow refund mechanics as Karthik proposed
4) Usage spike protection is acceptable with a tiered adjustment clause (we prefer a 2-quarter window to reconcile)

Requested ask: if Redwood can route the final DocuSign envelope today, Novamed will aim to sign within 72 hours. SOW attached for reference (Novamed_SOW_v2.pdf).

Evelyn Rios
VP, Strategic Accounts
Novamed
Procurement contact: procurement@novamed.com
